evidence: The 2019 full-text DOI 10.3390/sym11091165 develops secure-total domination bounds; no coefficientwise Paley order-13/17 classification in inspected sections.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Double domination is a 2-tuple closed-neighborhood covering condition, while secure-total domination concerns legal single-guard replacements keeping open-neighborhood coverage. The latter implies the former in general; the reverse does not, as shown by C6. An existing formula for just one parameter does not imply coefficientwise equality or mobility.

value.rationale: The order-13/17 prime Paley pair is a natural low-order comparison of highly symmetric quadratic-residue graphs. Equivalence of complete secure-total and double-domination polynomials is a nontrivial all-subset equality (false in general), and the exact connectivity contrast between one large component and 68 isolated pairs resolves an independently motivated mobility question. Exact naturally indexed finite classifications may be useful without generalization to all orders.
